schema_class.description: A truth value.
schema_class.name: core:BoolValue

schema_class.description: A defined mathematical term that is not a distribution family, construction or parameter: the gamma function, the standard score, the moment generating function.
schema_class.name: stat:Concept

schema_class.description: A condition tree (D1 §7). Its node shapes are owned by the core Pydantic Condition union, discriminated on op; this class is the range that names it.
schema_class.name: core:Condition

schema_class.description: A date or date-time kept verbatim as ISO 8601.
schema_class.name: core:DateValue

schema_class.description: Things that have a distribution and its characteristics.
schema_class.name: stat:Distributed

schema_class.description: A named family of probability distributions, possibly with parameters: the normal distribution, the gamma distribution, the standard normal distribution. Mentions include adjectival forms ("normally distributed", "has a gamma distribution").
schema_class.name: stat:DistributionFamily

schema_class.description: Base of every entity class; instances are D1 entities.
schema_class.name: core:Entity

schema_class.description: A reference to an entity: a batch local ref, or an entity key once stored. It is a position type, not a value; a slot whose range is an entity class takes it.
schema_class.name: core:EntityRef

schema_class.description: A permissible value of a schema enum.
schema_class.name: core:EnumValue

examples: scale family associated with the given distribution
annotations.title: family construction

schema_class.description: A way of generating a family of distributions from a base distribution, such as the location-scale family, the location family or the scale family associated with a distribution, or the general exponential family. Not itself a single distribution family.
schema_class.name: stat:FamilyConstruction

schema_class.description: A parameter of a distribution family or construction, such as the location parameter, the scale parameter, the shape parameter k, the rate, the mean or the standard deviation when these parameterize the family.
schema_class.name: stat:FamilyParameter

schema_class.description: A formula as written, with its symbol bindings (D1 §6.1).
schema_class.name: core:Formula

schema_class.description: An interval of values; an absent bound is unbounded.
schema_class.name: core:IntervalValue

schema_class.description: One entry of a map qualifier (ci:object map): a string key and a value. A map qualifier ranges over a subclass, multivalued and inlined, and is written as an object from key to value.
schema_class.name: core:MapEntry

schema_class.description: A number with its unit and basis as stated (D1 §6.2).
schema_class.name: core:NumberValue

schema_class.description: One entry of a param_mapping map: key the target family's parameter canonical name, value the canonical name of the base family's parameter it corresponds to.
schema_class.name: stat:ParamMapping

schema_class.description: One entry of a param_values or param_symbols map: key a canonical parameter name, value the formula it takes.
schema_class.name: stat:ParamValue

schema_class.description: Things that have parameters, a family or a construction.
schema_class.name: stat:Parameterized

schema_class.description: Text kept but not interpreted. The model-facing form names the sentence it lies in; the stored form adds the offsets the quote cascade located.
schema_class.name: core:PhraseValue

schema_class.description: A random variable denoted by a symbol (X, Y, Z, X_1, W) or by an expression in other random variables (a + b X, e^Y, X_1 + X_2). Local to the statement or section that introduces it.
schema_class.name: stat:RandomVariable

schema_class.description: A set written in LaTeX, such as \R, (0, \infty) or \R \setminus \{0\}.
schema_class.name: core:SetExpr

schema_class.description: An authored unit of meaning: a definition, theorem, proof, example, exercise, remark, convention or assumption. Claims belong to statements as premises, conclusions, definientia or example values. Listed in a batch's statements[], never in entities[].
schema_class.name: core:Statement

schema_class.description: How one symbol of a formula is bound (D1 §6.1).
schema_class.name: core:SymbolBinding

schema_class.description: Free text that is the value itself.
schema_class.name: core:TextValue

schema_class.description: Base of the D1 value classes. Every value carries the tag t, which names its class; the core Pydantic value union is discriminated on it.
schema_class.name: core:Value

schema_rule.description: A formula or set object parses under its slot's declared kind; the grammar's reading of a different kind (a set in a Formula slot, a relation where a formula belongs) is a warning, and the value is kept as written. Reads the grammar's parse, so it runs at finalize only.

schema_rule.check_expr: $all([not (b.symbol in claim.given_by_others and b.bind in ['free', 'family_param'] and not (b.symbol in claim.gives_symbols) and not ('family_structure' in claim.groups and b.bind == 'family_param')) for b in claim.bindings])
schema_rule.description: A symbol another claim gives as a parameter value binds param_of, not free or family_param, unless the claim is about the family as such (guideline §10.7 rows 2-4).
A formula that defines a variable or generates a family excludes the variable it defines (guideline §10.7).
A claim's modality follows from its statement_role (guideline §10.6).
schema_rule.when_expr: not ('structural' in claim.groups) and claim.statement_role != null

schema_rule.description: Formula and family-structure claims carry no claim nodes, only restrictions on their own symbols (guideline §10.7 rule 2).
A parameter_role claim is stated only when the role differs from the canonical name (guideline §10.4).

schema_rule.check_expr: $all([n.op == 'and' or (n.op == 'member' and (n.x_latex ?? '') in claim.subject.index_symbols) for n in claim.condition_nodes])
schema_rule.description: Premises and example values carry no conditions except the range of an index they are stated for; restrictions go to the claims that depend on them (guideline §10.7 rule 1).
schema_rule.when_expr: not ('structural' in claim.groups) and claim.statement_role in ['premise', 'example_value']

schema_rule.check_expr: claim.statement_premises.is_empty or $any([p in claim.claim_refs for p in claim.statement_premises])
schema_rule.description: Every other claim carries a claim node for the premises it depends on: it references at least one premise of its statement or of a context-premise assumption (guideline §10.7 rule 3).
schema_rule.when_expr: not ('structural' in claim.groups or 'formula_definition' in claim.groups or 'family_structure' in claim.groups) and not (claim.statement_role in ['premise', 'example_value'])

schema_rule.description: A claim's statement_role is one its statement's kind gives (guideline §10.3).
schema_rule.when_expr: not ('structural' in claim.groups) and claim.statement_kind != null

schema_rule.description: Structural claims carry no conditions (guideline §10.7 rule 4).
Structural claims take no statement_role and are asserted (guideline §10.3, §10.6).
Symbol-map keys are written without backslash (guideline §10.7).
The object parses as a set (parse ok under the set kind); otherwise a warning, and the object is kept as written. Reads the grammar's parse status, so it runs at finalize only.
The subject of has_parameter is not a random variable. Subsumed by the predicate's domain (Parameterized) once the side-table type check runs; kept as the check of the $is_a builtin.

schema_rule.check_expr: $all([o in claim.alternative_of for o in claim.same_slot])
schema_rule.description: At most one asserted or defined stated has_distribution per variable per statement, unless the claims are marked as alternatives; derived claims are exempt.

schema_rule.check_expr: $all([k in claim.family_params or k in $enums['ParameterRole'] for k in (claim.qualifiers.param_values ?? {}).keys])
schema_rule.description: Every param_values key is the canonical name of a parameter the family has in this run, or a ParameterRole value. A family's parameters are complete only at finalize.
